answer: Sybil defense in an AI agent economy works by pricing each identity above its profit. To join, an agent must forge a signed claim tying its execution history to one address, then post a deposit larger than what one extra persona can earn. N clones therefore lock N deposits while rewards per identity stay flat, so the attacker's cost rises linearly and the expected gain drops to zero or below. Any shared relic between two identities, such as identical telemetry or execution traces, triggers slashing of the whole cluster. Cloning becomes a canyon of losses deeper than honest work.
